'''Philosophy of Pseudoscience: Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem''' is a set of 23 essays that wrestle with the [[demarcation problem]] which is the question of how to distinguish between science and non-science. The book's editors are the notable [[Massimo Pigliucci]] and [[Maarten Boudry]]. It was published in August 2013 by the [[University of Chicago Press]]. <ref name=Turner>{{cite journal | doi=10.1086/676054 | title=Philosophy of Pseudoscience: Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem. Edited by Massimo Pigliucci and Maarten Boudry. Chicago (Illinois): University of Chicago Press. $35.00 (Paper). Viii + 469 p.; index. {{text|ISBN}}: 978-0-226-05179-6 (Hc); 978-0-226-05196-3 (Pb); 978-0-226-05182-6 (Eb). 2013. | year=2014 | last1=Turner | first1=Derek D. | journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology | volume=89 | issue=2 | pages=161–162 }}</ref><ref name=Ambasciano>{{cite journal | doi=10.1558/jcsr.27091 | title=Mapping Pluto's Republic: Cognitive and Epistemological Reflections on ''Philosophy of Pseudoscience: Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem'' | year=2017 | last1=Ambasciano | first1=Leonardo | journal=Journal for the Cognitive Science of Religion | volume=3 | issue=2 | pages=183–205 }}</ref><ref name=Nola>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s11016-014-9970-z | title=The fuzziness of pseudoscience | year=2015 | last1=Nola | first1=Robert | journal=Metascience | volume=24 | issue=2 | pages=279–284 | s2cid=254792704 }}</ref><ref name=Tatarczak>{{cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/roczfiloannaphilo.63.4.231 | last1=Tatarczak | first1=Michał | title=Reviewed work: Philosophy of Pseudoscience. Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem, Massimo Pigliucci i Maarten Boudry | journal=Roczniki Filozoficzne / Annales de Philosophie / Annals of Philosophy | year=2015 | volume=63 | issue=4 | pages=231–239 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | doi=10.7208/chicago/9780226051826.001.0001 | title=Philosophy of Pseudoscience | year=2013 | last1=Pigliucci | first1=Massimo | last2=Boudry | first2=Maarten | isbn=978-0-226-05196-3 }} {{isbn|978-0-226-05196-3}}</ref>

==Reception==
Derek D. Turner writing for ''[[The Quarterly Review of Biology]]'' says, "... this volume is well motivated. It would have benefitted, however, from the inclusion of someone representing and updating Laudan’s antidemarcationist perspective."<ref name=Turner/> ''[[Skeptical Inquirer]]'' magazine says, " The editors argue convincingly that the nature of science and the difference between science and pseudoscience are topics of crucial interest for philosophers, historians, and sociologists of science and also intrinsically interesting and directly relevant to people's lives."<ref name=skeptic>"Philosophy of Pseudoscience: Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem." (2013, November-December). ''Skeptical Inquirer'', '''37'''(6), 58, {{Gale|A348785702}} Accessed June 27, 2026.</ref> ''[[CHOICE magazine|Choice magazine]]'' says, "If the philosophical problem of demarcating science from pseudoscience has a stale reputation, this book is a revitalizing gust of fresh air."<ref name=choice>Martin, J. D. "Philosophy of Pseudoscience: Reconsidering the Demarcation Problem." Choice 51.6 (2014): 1027. {{ProQuest|1511595319}}. Accessed June 27, 2026.</ref>
